evidence: src/auth-google/auth-google.controller.ts: AuthGoogleController.login(loginDto: AuthGoogleLoginDto) returns this.authService.validateSocialLogin('google', await this.authGoogleService.getProfileByToken(loginDto)). The controller only delegates and contains no token or user logic.

src/auth-google/auth-google.module.ts: AuthGoogleModule declares imports [ConfigModule, AuthModule], providers [AuthGoogleService], controllers [AuthGoogleController] and exports [AuthGoogleService]. This is wiring for the same Google-auth feature.
Both files are about Google login only. No unrelated endpoints or providers appear, and no validation or auth rule is repeated across the two files.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: The unit handles a single concern: the presentation entry point for Google social login. auth-google.module.ts only wires up AuthGoogleController and AuthGoogleService, and it imports AuthModule to get AuthService. auth-google.controller.ts has one endpoint. That endpoint gets the Google profile from AuthGoogleService.getProfileByToken and passes it to AuthService.validateSocialLogin. Token verification and the social-login/user rules stay in their services. The controller does not repeat them and does not go around them, for example by checking tokens or creating users itself. The two files use the module's abstractions consistently, and no rule or invariant is duplicated.
